finding.claim: SQL injection: the unvalidated $_GET['sort'] value is concatenated into the ORDER BY clause of a query run with PDO::query(). ORDER BY cannot be parameterized, and the allowlist used in list_users_safe() is not applied here. An attacker can inject a subquery or CASE expression to infer data from any table in the SQLite DB, for example via a boolean or error-based blind technique.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter $_GET['sort'] (list.php:5), attacker-controlled, no authentication seen
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: $sort concatenated directly into SQL and executed via query()

finding.guards_checked: Checked for an allowlist, casting, escaping, prepared statements, and auth/middleware on the path: none apply in list_users_sorted(). Only list_users_safe() (lines 9-13) uses an allowlist map, and it is a separate function. Whether list_users_sorted() is actually called or routed could not be determined, since list.php is the only application file and nothing in it calls the function; the vulnerable function is reachable if any entry point invokes it. find_user() (lines 15-19) uses a prepared statement and is safe.

verdict.guard_found: none in list_users_sorted(); the allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in the separate function list_users_safe(), and find_user() uses a prepared statement
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (list.php:5 reads raw $_GET['sort'] and list.php:6 concatenates it into ORDER BY via query() with no guard), but list.php only defines functions and nothing calls list_users_sorted(), so reachability by an attacker can't be determined from the code available.
